solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Directly hit twice

blocks.note: one kind of hit, with the open hand
the second hit, a sharp blow

explanation.surface: Someone struck squarely, and more than once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' asks for two different words that each mean hit, set one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap-bang is an informal adverb meaning exactly or squarely, as in landing right in the middle of something.

clue.text: Secured case of champagne guarded by boy

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the outermost letters are wanted
what is guarded is surrounded by its guard, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A boy keeps watch over a secured case of champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of champagne' looks like a crate of bottles, but it means the word's shell, its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoes or a corset that are laced have been tied up and fastened, so made secure.

clue.text: Father on social media site? Man is careful

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
short for Instagram
a man in chess, one of the pieces

explanation.surface: A dad posting online is warned that a man must be cautious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places father first in a down answer. 'Man' is a chess man, a playing piece, here the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone painstaking takes great pains, working with thorough attention to detail.

clue.text: Pastry a very quiet Greek character consumed in shelter

indicators.note: food consumed goes inside, so one piece is swallowed by another

blocks.note: taken as written
pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet
the lee is the sheltered side
a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A pastry, eaten very quietly by a Greek person hiding in a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' sounds like a person from Greece but is a letter of its alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple pie is a baked dish of fruit encased in pastry, so it is an example of a pastry.

clue.text: Finally addressing being active, couple announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out to listeners, so we want what is heard

blocks.note: an idiom for moving about busily
a couple is two

explanation.surface: A busy couple at last make an announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple announced' sounds like news of a pair, but it asks for the spoken word for the number of a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To get around to a job is to deal with it at last after delay, so finally addressing it.

clue.text: Queen carried in taxi close to getting irritable

indicators.note: a passenger carried in a vehicle sits inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
R for Regina, Latin for queen
by means near, as in 'standing by the door'

explanation.surface: The Queen, riding in a cab, is getting tetchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like it wants a last letter, but here it means near. R is the Regina of royal signatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby is an informal adjective for bad-tempered and grumpy, the mood of someone easily annoyed.

clue.text: Elegant girl in Cyprus

indicators.note: being in a place means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A stylish young woman on the island of Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: CY is the country code used for Cyprus, on vehicles and web domains.
explanation.definitionFit: Classy is an informal adjective for stylish and sophisticated, showing high quality in appearance or manner.

clue.text: Sailor has sunken top craft

indicators.note: in a down answer the top letter sinks to the bottom, so the first letter moves to the end

blocks.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor's boat has sunk, its top under water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a ship to go with the sailor, but here it means skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Art and craft both mean skill in making things, a learned technique or trade.

clue.text: Go-between’s business is out of money? Madness!

blocks.note: broke means having no money
rage is a fit of madness, fury

explanation.surface: An outraged cry that an agent's firm has gone bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and exclamation make two separate sentences, but the pieces simply join in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker is an agent acting between buyer and seller; brokerage is that trade or the firm carrying it on.

clue.text: I’m coming in for article of waste to be sparing

indicators.note: coming in for someone is replacing them, so one piece swaps out another

blocks.note: scrap is waste material
the indefinite article
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone stepping in to replace an item of rubbish in order to save.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article of waste' reads as a piece of rubbish, but 'article' is the word A, swapped out of the word for waste.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is a verb meaning to economise severely, spending as little money as possible.

clue.text: Grip carton tight, keeping it overturned

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so the letters run the other way
tight is slang for drunk, and drunk letters stagger into a new order
to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hold a carton tightly so it does not tip over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' seems to describe the grip, but it is the slang for drunk that signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Traction is the adhesive friction of a tyre or foot on a surface, which is its grip.

clue.text: Parent cycling son joins

indicators.note: going round a cycle moves the front letter to the back

blocks.note: dad is a parent
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A father out cycling is joined by his son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' looks like riding a bike; it means the first letter goes round to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To add something is to put it together with another thing, so adds and joins are synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: English girl and a priest uncovered spies

indicators.note: uncovering strips off the outer layer, so the outside letters go

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a miss is a girl
taken as written
the word to lose its outside letters

explanation.surface: An English girl and a clergyman are unmasked as secret agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' sounds like exposure of the spies, but it strips the outer letters from the clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Emissaries are agents sent on a mission, sometimes secret, so a loose stand-in for covert agents.

clue.text: House acquired by poor saddler in US state

indicators.note: something in poor shape is damaged, so the letters are broken and reformed
what is acquired is taken in, so one piece ends up inside another

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A struggling saddle-maker buys a house in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link to the definition, but its letters join the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhode Island is the smallest of the fifty American states, in New England.

clue.text: Emptying circle a ringmaster goes around

indicators.note: the clue words go around the answer, enclosing it within them

blocks.note: the answer runs across these three words

explanation.surface: A circus ringmaster parades round the ring as the crowd leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circle' and 'goes around' suggest circular motion, but the answer sits inside the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing a room or table is taking everything off it, so emptying it.

clue.text: Some distance until dog collapsed close to me

indicators.note: something collapsed has fallen apart, so the letters are rebuilt in a different order
the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dog walks a long way before collapsing near the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some distance' is the definition, loosely: longitude is a distance east or west measured in degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Longitude is angular position east or west of Greenwich, a measure of how far round the globe a place lies.

clue.text: Fine starters from oyster kitchen are yummy

indicators.note: starters are what come first, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A restaurant review: the oyster starters from this kitchen are delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' plays on the first course of a meal, which oysters often are.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay and fine are both informal ways of saying satisfactory or acceptable.

clue.text: Keep fiddles before hosting summit for violinists

indicators.note: a summit is the top, and in a word the top is its first letter
a host has guests inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: cons are swindles, which are fiddles
ere is an old word for before
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Violinists are told to keep their fiddles before a top-level meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddles' next to 'violinists' means violins in the surface, but here it means swindles, which are cons.
explanation.definitionFit: To conserve is to preserve or save something from waste or loss, so to keep it.

clue.text: Opponent cannot win regularly

indicators.note: doing something regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A rival who consistently fails to win.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignore the space between the words and take every second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is a person opposed to a policy or cause, so an opponent of it.

clue.text: Old enclosure surround by grass is unlocked once again

indicators.note: a thing surrounded has something all round it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass
O is the abbreviation for old
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: An old animal pen ringed by long grass has its gate unbarred again.
explanation.walkthrough: The grass word is split around the old enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Reopened means opened again after closure, and opening a locked thing is unlocking it.

clue.text: Be very cold following winds, when exposed

indicators.note: exposing something takes its outer layer away, so the outside letters drop

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
breezes are light winds

explanation.surface: You feel the chill when out in the open after the wind gets up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exposed' sounds like being out in the weather but means stripping the outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeze is to feel extremely chilly, as in 'I'm freezing out here'.

clue.text: Alcohol good with unlimited herb crackers and biscuits

indicators.note: with no limits means without its boundaries, so the end letters go

blocks.note: gin is an alcoholic spirit
G is the abbreviation for good
the word to lose its first and last letters
crackers and nuts both mean crazy

explanation.surface: A party spread: drinks, unlimited herb crackers and a plate of biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' sits among the snacks as a food but is British slang for mad. Ginger nuts are hard ginger-flavoured British biscuits.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger nuts are a familiar type of crunchy ginger cookie, so an example of biscuits.

clue.text: Say when retiring is wise

indicators.note: retiring is withdrawing or going back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, which is what 'say' can mean
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Knowing when to stop and retire is a mark of wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say when' is what a host says while pouring a drink; here 'say' is the for-example sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage is an adjective for having deep wisdom and sound judgement, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Wind energy mostly environmentally- friendly

indicators.note: most of something is all but a bit, so the last letter is dropped
to wind is to twist and turn, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: the word without its final letter

explanation.surface: Wind power is mostly an eco-friendly source of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as the noun of wind power; as a verb rhyming with 'find' it signals the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is the everyday label for policies or products that protect nature and the ecology.

clue.text: Aquatic plant, nothing small, ultimately spread

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter is taken

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket
wee is Scottish for small
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tiny pond plant that in the end spreads over everything.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman out without scoring makes a duck, so duck means nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Duckweed is a tiny floating plant that covers the surface of still ponds, so a water plant.

clue.text: Use needles knocking out new teamwear

indicators.note: knocking something out removes it, so a letter goes

blocks.note: knitting is working with needles
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone knits a new set of team shirts.
explanation.walkthrough: Kit is the British word for a sports team's uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A team's kit is the matching shirts, shorts and socks its players wear, so its sportswear outfit.

clue.text: Visibly embarrassed admitting row sounded ferocious

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece is let inside another

blocks.note: going red shows embarrassment
an oar is what you row with

explanation.surface: Red-faced, someone owns up that a quarrel turned savage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' tempts as a quarrel, but it is the rowing kind, giving the blade you pull.
explanation.definitionFit: To roar is to make a loud deep fierce cry, the sound of a lion, so roared means sounded savage.

clue.text: Bothersome thing, extremely lamentable grinding tool

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so its first and last letters

blocks.note: a pest is a nuisance
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A tiresome, truly awful tool for grinding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'lamentable' but takes only the word's ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestle is the club-shaped implement used with a mortar to crush and pound spices.

clue.text: Concluded fellow back in alehouse exaggerated

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so its final letter is used

blocks.note: over means finished
a don is a fellow of a university college
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man in a pub at closing time, having overdone it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in' suggests a reversal or insertion, but it just picks the last letter. A don is an Oxford or Cambridge college fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdone is carried too far or overstated, as with a performance or praise.
